translation: (The meaning of heat being repletion and cold being vacuity also originates from the Inner Canon, speaking of the primordial qi by which the human body arises; the Master instead speaks of it in terms of the generation and control of the Five Phases. The principles of both are both worth investigating; neither may be mutually denied.) Generally, the Lungs are originally clear; when vacuous, they become warm. The Heart is originally hot; when vacuous, it becomes cold. The Liver is originally warm; when vacuous, it becomes clear. The Spleen is originally damp; when vacuous, it becomes dry. The Kidneys are originally cold; when vacuous, they become hot. Supposing that cold stomach is vacuity: this is because the yin water and cold qi within the stomach are excessive in repletion, while the yang fire and hot qi are weakened and vacuous; it is not that the damp qi of the stomach earth is originally weakened. (This passage's argument is precise; this is what is meant by each of the Five Phases having yin and yang.) Hence one should warmly supplement the decline of the yang fire within the stomach and retreat the excess of its yin water and cold qi. Again, for example, stomach heat being repletion: this is because the yang fire within the stomach is replete and the yin water is vacuous; hence one should use cold medicines to drain the replete fire within the stomach and nourish its vacuous water.
translator_notes: 先生 (the Master) refers to the author Liu Wansu.
